answer: Admission requires 1,000 units of compute-proof-work per identity to serve as a secure inlet for the network. The verifier treats each hash like a ripple spreading across the ledger to validate uniqueness. While an honest agent pays this cost once, an attacker spawning 1,000 fakes must solve 1,000,000 puzzles, facing a zephyr of computational exhaustion. Fraud triggers a permanent identity burn, though the mechanism assumes no pooled hashing.
